'''Franz Wagner''' (born 27 August 2001) is a German [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. Listed at {{convert|6|ft|9|in|m|2}} and {{convert|220|lbs|kg|0}}, he plays the [[small forward]] position.

Wagner, a native of [[Berlin]], started his career with [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL) club [[Alba Berlin]]. In 2019, he was named [[Basketball Bundesliga Best German Young Player|BBL Best German Young Player]]. Wagner has played for the German youth national teams, winning a gold medal at the 2018 [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]]. 

His older brother [[Moritz Wagner (basketball)|Moritz Wagner]], a former Michigan standout, plays for the [[Orlando Magic]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).

==Early career==
In the 2018–19 season, Wagner played on a dual contract for both [[Alba Berlin]] in the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL), top German league, and SSV Lokomotive Bernau in the third-tier [[ProB]] league. In May 2019, he won the [[Basketball Bundesliga Best German Young Player|BBL Best Young Player Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.easycredit-bbl.de/de/n/news/2019/mai/franz-wagner--bester-deutscher-nachwuchsspieler-u22-/|title=easyCredit - Franz Wagner|work=www.easycredit-bbl.de|accessdate=13 May 2019}}</ref> In Game 2 of the BBL Finals against [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]], Wagner scored a team-high 14 points, making all six of his shots.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.easycredit-bbl.de/de/n/spielberichte/2018-2019/nachbericht/2019-06-19-ber-fcb/|title=Bayern vor der Titelverteidigung? München holt sich mit 82:77 in Berlin den zweiten Sieg in der Finalserie|work=www.easycredit-bbl.de|accessdate=21 June 2019}}</ref> By the end of the season, he was averaging 4.6 points in 12.4 minutes per game in the BBL and played limited minutes in the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].<ref name="realgm">{{cite web |title=Franz Wagner Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Franz-Wagner/Summary/108861 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=2 September 2019}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Wagner was considered a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].<ref name="rivals">{{cite web |title=Franz Wagner, 2019 Small forward |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2019/franz-wagner-256171 |publisher=[[Rivals.com]] |accessdate=1 September 2019}}</ref><ref name="247sports">{{cite web |title=Franz Wagner, Germany, Small Forward |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Franz-Wagner-46056818/high-school-219589/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |accessdate=1 September 2019}}</ref> Among the [[NCAA Division I]] programs that recruited him were [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]], [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], and [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]].<ref name="daniels">{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=German star Franz Wagner considering college, pro options |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/German-star-Franz-Wagner-considering-college-pro-options-129733913/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |accessdate=1 September 2019 |date=5 March 2019}}</ref> On July 6, 2019, Wagner committed to play [[college basketball]] for Michigan under head coach [[Juwan Howard]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2019/7/6/mens-basketball-german-guard-franz-wagner-signs-will-join-wolverines-this-fall.aspx|title=German Guard Franz Wagner Signs, Will Join Wolverines This Fall|website=University of Michigan Athletics|language=en|access-date=7 July 2019}}</ref> In doing so, he turned down an opportunity to sign a professional contract with Alba Berlin.<ref name=sz>{{cite web |title=Franz Wagner in Michigan - "Ich musste selber entscheiden" |url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/sport/franz-wagner-alba-college-basketball-1.4523023-2 |website=[[Süddeutsche Zeitung]] |accessdate=1 September 2019 |language=German |date=16 July 2019}}</ref>

===Sophomore===
During his sophomore season, Wagner posted 14 double-figure games and four 20+ point games, he averaged 13.0 points per game with 6.3 rebounds, a team-high 30 steals and a second-best 23 blocks. Following the season he was named second-team All-Big Ten by the coaches and third-team by the media. <ref>https://michigan.rivals.com/news/franz-wagner-s-stock-continues-to-skyrocket-in-latest-nba-draft-projections</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://bigten.org/news/2021/3/9/general-2020-21-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx |title=2020-21 Big Ten Men's Basketball Postseason Honors Announced |website=BigTen.org |date=9 March 2021 |access-date=9 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/9/mens-basketball-dickinson-howard-headline-big-ten-awards-as-top-freshman-coach.aspx |title=Dickinson, Howard Headline Big Ten Awards as Top Freshman, Coach |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |accessdate=9 March 2021 |date=9 March 2021 |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On May 4, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] forgoing his remaining college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31387924/michigan-wolverines-franz-wagner-decides-enter-nba-draft|title=Michigan Wolverines' Franz Wagner enters 2021 NBA draft|author=Wojnarowski, Adrian |accessdate=May 9, 2021|date=May 4, 2021 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:Franz Wagner (basketball).jpg|thumb|Wagner with the [[Germany national under-19 basketball team|German U18 team]] at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]] in 2018]]
Wagner played for [[Germany national under-17 basketball team|Germany]] at the [[2017 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in [[Podgorica]], Montenegro. In five games, he averaged 7.4 points per game as his team finished in 13th place.<ref>{{cite web |title=Franz Jacob Wagner (GER)'s profile - FIBA U16 European Championship Division A 2017 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u16/2017/player/Franz-Jacob-Wagner |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=2 September 2019}}</ref> In 2018, Wagner averaged six points per game and helped Germany win the gold medal at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]], an under-18 competition in [[Mannheim]], Germany.<ref name="sang">{{cite web |last1=Sang |first1=Orion |title=Franz Wagner, brother of Moritz, picks Wolverines |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2019/07/06/michigan-basketball-recruiting-franz-wagner/1537637001/ |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |accessdate=2 September 2019 |date=6 July 2019}}</ref> In the [[2019 FIBA U18 European Championship]] in [[Volos]], Greece, he averaged 13 points and 4.8 rebounds per game, leading his team to 11th place. He missed one game with a back injury.<ref name="burkhardt">{{cite web |last1=Burkhardt |first1=Dylan |title=What we learned about Franz Wagner at FIBA U18 Euros |url=https://umhoops.com/2019/08/05/what-we-learned-about-franz-wagner-at-fiba-u18-euros/ |publisher=UM Hoops |accessdate=2 September 2019 |date=5 August 2019}}</ref>
